replies.body:
UAE National Day and Eid hours on Google for salons

Set special hours on your Google profile for 2 and 3 December now, because National Day has fixed dates. For Eid, wait until the days are announced after the moon sighting, then add each day the same way.

By Kabsi. Published 16 November 2026. 7 min read

Checked against Google's help pages and the other sources below on 8 November 2026. 
In short
National Day is 2 and 3 December, a Wednesday and a Thursday in 2026. Eid follows the moon sighting, so set it once the days are announced, not from a calendar printed months ahead.
Special hours change up to 6 days in a row and leave your normal week as it is.
A late opening on the evening before Eid is special hours too, so clients see it.

2. How do I set National Day hours on my profile?
3. Should I set special hours if I am open as normal?
4. When should I set my Eid hours on Google?
5. What about late nights before Eid and National Day?
6. Do Ramadan hours work the same way?
7. What if a client finds us closed, or Google changes our hours?
8. What Kabsi does here
9. Questions owners ask
10. Sources
Which UAE holidays should a salon plan hours for?

The UAE government portal lists the public holidays for the public and private sectors: New Year on 1 January, Eid Al Fitr, Arafah Day, Eid Al Adha, the Hijri New Year, the Prophet Mohammed's birthday, and National Day on 2 and 3 December. Every one of them except New Year and National Day is set by the moon sighting.

National Day: 2 and 3 December, two days. In 2026 that is Wednesday 2 and Thursday 3 December.
Eid Al Fitr: from 1 to 3 Shawwal. The portal says that if Ramadan lasts 30 days, day 30 is also an official holiday for Eid Al Fitr.
Arafah Day and Eid Al Adha: 9 Thu Al Hijjah, then 10 to 12 Thu Al Hijjah.
Hijri New Year: 1 Muharram. The Prophet's birthday: 12 Rabi' Awwal.

The portal also says that, under Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024, a public holiday is not moved to another day when it falls on a weekend or on another public holiday. Whether your salon or barbershop opens on these days is your decision. What matters on Google is that your profile says what you decided, before clients start checking.

How do I set National Day hours on my profile?

Sign in to the Google Account linked to your profile, select Edit profile, then Hours, and next to Special hours select Edit. Add 2 December and 3 December, then leave Closed ticked or untick it and enter the hours you will open.

1
Go to your Business Profile.
2
Select Edit profile, then Hours.
3
In the Business hours section, next to Special hours, select Edit.
4
For a date Google suggests, select Review. For another day, select Add a date and enter it.
5
Closed all day: leave the Closed box ticked. Open: untick Closed and enter your times.
6
Select Save.

Google's own holiday list for the UAE, read on 8 November 2026, shows 2 December but not 3 December, so add the 3rd yourself with Add a date. Google says special hours show on your profile only if your business hours are set to Open with main hours, so check that first. After saving, you find the dates under Special hours in Edit profile.

Should I set special hours if I am open as normal?

Yes, it is worth the minute it takes. Google says that on the holidays it lists, a warning may appear on your profile telling people your hours might differ, and that it is a good idea to confirm your hours for official holidays even when they match your regular hours.

Google's list for the UAE also includes 30 November (Commemoration Day) and, in January 2027, 1 January and two days for Isra and Mi'raj. Of these, only 1 January is on the government portal's list of public holidays, so a warning may show on days your salon is open as usual. To confirm normal hours, add the date under Special hours, untick Closed and enter your usual times.

When should I set my Eid hours on Google?

Once the days are announced. The portal says Eid Al Fitr, Arafah Day and Eid Al Adha are determined by moon sighting, so a date you set weeks ahead from a printed calendar can be a day out, and clients who check your profile that morning would see the wrong answer.

1
Before Ramadan, decide your hours for each Eid day and for the evenings before.
2
When the moon sighting is announced, add each Eid day under Special hours with Add a date.
3
If the days move, open the date and change it. To take off a closed day, select Delete next to it; to take off an open day, select More, then Remove day.
4
The evening before Eid, open your profile on a phone and check what a client sees.

Closing for a week or more?

Google says special hours are for closures of up to 6 days in a row. If your salon closes for 7 days or more, or for a time you do not know yet, Google says to mark the business as Temporarily closed instead, and to reopen it on the profile when you are back.
What about late nights before Eid and National Day?

Set them as special hours too. A late opening the evening before Eid changes your hours for one day, and Google says special hours are for days when your business temporarily adjusts its hours, as well as for holidays and special events.

For a day with a break, select More, then Add hours, and enter a second set of times. Google's own example of a break is open 9 AM to 2 PM, then again 5 PM to 10 PM. If you take bookings online, close the same times in your booking system on the same day, so a client does not book a slot your profile says is closed.

A short Update post can say the days and the times, with a Book button to your booking page. Google says a post with a phone number in its text might be rejected if the number cannot be verified as the business's, and suggests a Call now button instead, which uses the phone number on your profile.

Do Ramadan hours work the same way?

No. Ramadan lasts about a month, much longer than the 6 days special hours are meant for, and Google's guidelines say you may use your current seasonal hours as your regular hours. So change your main hours for the month and add the Eid days as special hours.

Under Edit profile, Hours, change the times next to each day to your Ramadan hours before the month starts, and put your regular hours back after Eid. Google says that after you update your hours, a post on your profile may confirm the change, and you can edit or delete that post. The full walk-through, with the UK dates too, is in how to set holiday hours on Google.

What if a client finds us closed, or Google changes our hours?

Set or fix the special hours as soon as you know, even on the day. If someone suggests different hours on Google, Google may tell you first, and you have 4 days to accept or reject the suggestion.

Google says it may publish a suggested edit you have not answered when other public information, such as your website, supports it. Put your holiday hours on your website and in your booking page too, so they agree with your profile, and check your profile the morning after each holiday. If your normal week has changed, see someone changed my hours on Google.

What Kabsi does here

Five days before a UAE public holiday, Kabsi asks you by email, and in Kabsi under Hours, what your salon will do: normal hours, closed or custom hours. It never assumes. Closed or custom hours become special hours for those days once you tap Confirm and save to Google, and Kabsi checks that Google shows them. A holiday that follows the moon, such as Eid, is marked "expected", and you can move the days up to three either way. Ramadan is asked once, before the month starts: normal hours or different hours for the whole month.

On Hours you can also set a special day for any date, such as a late night before Eid. Kabsi checks your hours on Google every day and tells you when Google shows something different. Nothing goes on Google until you say yes. Run the free check.

Questions owners ask
Can I set National Day hours weeks in advance?
Yes. Google says you can set special hours in advance for the holidays it lists, and they show to customers only on those dates. National Day is always 2 and 3 December, so you can set it now.
Why not set Eid hours from this year's calendar?
Because the portal says Eid follows the moon sighting. A day set from a calendar can be a day out. Add the days once they are announced, and check your profile the evening before.

replies.body:
Christmas and bank holiday hours on Google for UK salons

Add every day from Christmas Eve to the first Monday of January under Special hours on your Google profile, open or closed, including the days you open as usual. Use your own nation's bank holidays: Scotland has two more than England and Wales over this period.

By Kabsi. Published 23 November 2026. 6 min read

Checked against Google's help pages and the other sources below on 8 November 2026. 
In short
Christmas Day is Friday 25 December 2026 and Boxing Day's bank holiday moves to Monday 28 December.
Scotland adds St Andrew's Day on 30 November and a 2nd January holiday on Monday 4 January 2027. Google may warn clients that your hours might differ on Christmas Eve and Saturday 26 December too.
Closed for 7 days or more in a row? Google says to mark the business temporarily closed.

Which dates do UK salons and barbers need this Christmas?

GOV.UK lists separate bank holidays for England and Wales, for Scotland and for Northern Ireland. Over Christmas and New Year 2026 all three share Christmas Day, the Boxing Day substitute day and New Year's Day, and Scotland adds two more days.

England and Wales, and Northern Ireland: Christmas Day, Friday 25 December 2026; Boxing Day (substitute day), Monday 28 December; New Year's Day, Friday 1 January 2027. Scotland: St Andrew's Day, Monday 30 November 2026; Christmas Day, Friday 25 December; Boxing Day (substitute day), Monday 28 December; New Year's Day, Friday 1 January 2027; 2nd January (substitute day), Monday 4 January 2027. 
GOV.UK says that when a bank holiday falls on a weekend, a substitute weekday becomes a bank holiday, normally the following Monday. Boxing Day 2026 is a Saturday, which is why its bank holiday is Monday 28 December, and 2 January 2027 is a Saturday, which is why Scotland's holiday is Monday 4 January. A salon in Glasgow and one in Belfast can have different answers on the same day, so check the list for your own nation.

Which days will Google flag on my profile?

Google keeps its own holiday list, and on those days a warning may appear on your profile telling people your hours might differ. Its UK list for this period includes Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day on Saturday 26 December, Boxing Day observed on Monday 28 December and New Year's Day.

For Scotland it also lists St Andrew's Day and 2nd January, with the observed day on 4 January. Christmas Eve and Saturday 26 December are not bank holidays, but they are on Google's list, and both are normally busy days for a salon or a barbershop.

Google says it is a good idea to confirm your hours for official holidays even when they are the same as your regular hours, so customers can see your special hours are accurate. If you open as normal on Saturday 26 December, add that date with your usual Saturday times.

How do I add Christmas hours to my Google profile?

Use special hours, which change chosen dates and leave your normal week as it is. Google says special hours are for holidays, special events and other exceptional circumstances, and for closures of up to 6 days in a row.

1
Sign in to the Google Account linked to your profile and go to your Business Profile.
2
Select Edit profile, then Hours.
3
Next to Special hours, select Edit.
4
For a date Google suggests, select Review. For any other day, select Add a date.
5
Leave Closed ticked for a day you are shut, or untick it and enter your times.
6
Select Save, then repeat for each date.

Google says special hours show only if your business hours are set to Open with main hours. You can add the dates now: Google says you can set special hours in advance for the holidays it lists, and they show to customers only on those dates.

How do I show late nights before Christmas?

Add each late night as a special hours date with your longer times. A salon open until 9 PM on a Thursday in December is a temporary change of hours for that day, which is what Google says special hours are for.

For a day with a break, select More, then Add hours, and enter the second set of times. A short Update post with a Book button can say which evenings you are open late. Google says a post with a phone number in its text might be rejected if the number cannot be verified as the business's, so use the Call now button, which uses the number on your profile.

If clients book online, change the same days in your booking system. When the two disagree, a client sees one answer on Google and another when they try to book.

What if we close for the whole Christmas break?

Count the days. Christmas Eve to New Year's Day is 9 days in a row, and Google says that for 7 or more days in a row, or for a closure of unknown length, you should mark the business as Temporarily closed rather than add special hours.

Up to 6 days, or 7 and more

Closed from Friday 25 December to Monday 28 December is 4 days: add each one as special hours. Closed from Thursday 24 December to Monday 4 January is 12 days: mark the business Temporarily closed under Edit profile, Hours, then reopen it when you are back.

Google says that marking a business temporarily closed helps people who search for you by name understand that the closure is only temporary. Put a date in your diary to reopen the profile on your first day back.

What if Google shows the wrong hours after Christmas?

Check your profile on a phone the first morning after each holiday. If someone has suggested different hours, Google may notify you, and you have 4 days to accept or reject the suggestion before Google may publish it.

Google says it may publish a suggested edit you have not answered when other public information, such as your website, supports it. Put the same Christmas hours on your website and booking page, and if your normal week changed, see someone changed my hours on Google. The steps for every other UK bank holiday in 2027 are in how to set holiday hours on Google.

What Kabsi does here

Five days before a bank holiday, Kabsi asks you by email, and in Kabsi under Hours, what your salon will do: normal hours, closed or custom hours. It never assumes. It uses the GOV.UK bank holidays for your own nation, read from your Google address, so a salon in Scotland is asked about St Andrew's Day and one in Northern Ireland gets its own dates. Closed or custom hours become special hours once you tap Confirm and save to Google, and Kabsi checks that Google shows them.

Christmas Eve and Saturday 26 December are not bank holidays, so set them yourself on Hours, where you can add a special day for any date, late nights included. Kabsi checks your hours on Google every day and tells you when Google shows something different. Nothing goes on Google until you say yes. Run the free check.

Questions owners ask
Do I need to set Boxing Day if I open on Saturday 26 December?
It helps. Boxing Day is on Google's holiday list, so a warning may show that your hours might differ. Add 26 December under Special hours with your usual Saturday times.
Is Christmas Eve a bank holiday?
No. It is not on the GOV.UK list for any UK nation, but it is on Google's UK holiday list, so confirm your hours for it under Special hours.

steps.sent: Guide page /guides/reply-to-bad-google-review-salon: How should a salon reply to a bad Google review?. Is every statement about Kabsi and about Google in this page true and consistent with the facts?

replies.body:
How should a salon reply to a bad Google review?

Reply within a day or two in three or four calm sentences: thank them, name the problem once, say what you can do, and ask them to get in touch through the details on your profile. When a review mentions a reaction, a burn or an injury, say nothing about what happened in public and speak to your insurer before you reply.

By Kabsi. Published 30 November 2026. 8 min read

Checked against Google's help pages on 8 November 2026. 
In short
A colour or a cut gone wrong: no argument about technique in public, and an offer to talk.
A long wait: say sorry once and explain only what is true.
A price complaint: point to the prices on your profile without arguing about the bill.
A reaction or an injury: a short, neutral reply at most, after you speak to your insurer.
See what Google shows about you

Type your business and Kabsi reads your Google profile and searches around it, like a customer.

Find your business on Google
Check my business free

Free check. No account and no Google access needed.

In this guide
1. Should a salon reply to a bad review at all?
2. How do I reply when a client hated their colour or cut?
3. What do I say when a client waited too long?
4. How do I answer a complaint about the price?
5. What if a review mentions an allergic reaction, a burn or an injury?
6. What should a salon never write in a reply?
7. When can I report a bad review instead?
8. What Kabsi does here
9. Questions owners ask
10. Sources
Should a salon reply to a bad review at all?

Yes. Google says replying shows customers you value their feedback, that negative reviews are not necessarily a sign of poor business practices, and that a constructive reply may even encourage the customer to update their review. The reply is mainly read by the next client deciding whether to book.

Google checks every reply against its content policies before it is posted, usually within 10 minutes but sometimes up to 30 days, and tells the reviewer when you reply. The reply shows as your business, not under your own name. Google also says a reviewer can still change their review after reading your reply. The general steps for any business are in how to respond to a negative Google review; this guide is about the reviews salons and barbers get.

How do I reply when a client hated their colour or cut?

Thank them, say you are sorry it was not what they wanted, and ask them to get in touch so you can talk it through. Do not explain in public why the colour lifted that way or whose fault it was: the reader sees a salon arguing with a client.

Example review, 1 star: "Asked for a soft caramel balayage and came out brassy orange. Paid a fortune." Reply: "Thank you for telling us, Hannah, and we are sorry the colour was not what you asked for. We would like to see it and talk about what we can do, so please get in touch through the details on our profile. Mia, salon owner"

If you offer a correction appointment or a refund, do it privately, and never in return for changing or removing the review. Google's policy says businesses must not offer incentives, such as payment, discounts or free services, in exchange for a review or for revising or removing a negative one.

What do I say when a client waited too long?

Say sorry once and explain only what is true and useful, such as a running late policy or how you now let clients know. Google's advice is to be honest, acknowledge mistakes, and not take responsibility for things outside your control.

Example review, 2 stars: "Booked for 2pm, sat for 35 minutes before anyone started. Nobody said a word." Reply: "We are sorry, Omar. A 35 minute wait without a word from us is not good enough. When a barber is running late we now message clients before they arrive. Please get in touch through our profile if you would like to talk about it. The Fade Room" Write the line about messaging clients only if you really do it. A reply that promises a change you never make reads worse a month later.

How do I answer a complaint about the price?

Do not argue about the bill in public. Thank them, say where your prices are shown, and invite them to get in touch about their visit. If prices start from a figure and depend on hair length or time, say that plainly once.

Example review, 2 stars: "Quoted one price, charged nearly double for a cut and blow dry." Reply: "Thank you for the feedback, Sarah. Our prices are listed on our profile, and longer hair takes more time, which our stylists explain before they start. We are sorry if that did not happen at your visit. Please get in touch so we can look at it. Rose Lane Salon"

Google lets salons list services with prices on the profile, under Edit services, and says a customer reviewing a service business may be asked to choose the service they had. Keeping that list accurate answers many price questions before they become reviews. The steps are in how to add services and prices to Google.

What if a review mentions an allergic reaction, a burn or an injury?

Treat it differently from every other bad review. Do not discuss what happened, the products, a patch test or any medical detail in public, do not admit or deny fault in the reply, and speak to your insurer before you write anything. Then reply briefly and take it private.

1
Do not reply in the first hour. Read it, then save a copy with the date.
2
Write down what your records show: the appointment, the products, any patch test and who did the work. Keep it private.
3
Call your insurer or adviser and ask how they want you to respond. This guide is not legal advice.
4
If you reply, keep it short and neutral, with no details of the treatment, and ask the client to get in touch through the details on your profile.
5
Have the conversation in private, by phone or email, not under the review.

Google's own tip for complex situations is to protect the reviewer's privacy and politely ask them to contact you by phone or email to resolve it privately. Its content policy also does not allow posting someone's medical information, so a reply that discusses the client's skin or scalp in detail can do harm on more than one front.

A holding reply, for example

"Thank you for letting us know. We take this seriously and would like to speak with you directly. Please contact us through the details on our profile. Rose Lane Salon"
What should a salon never write in a reply?

Anything that makes the next reader trust you less: an argument, a client's private details, a discount for changing the review, or blame on a named member of staff. Google says never to share a reviewer's private information or engage in personal attacks.

Do

Thank them, even when it stings.
Name the problem in one sentence.
Point to the details on your profile so they can reach you.
Sign as the salon or the owner.

Do not

Write their appointment details, phone number or what they paid.
Say they were rude or that it never happened.
Offer a discount or a free service to change or remove the review.
Blame a stylist or a barber by name in public.
When can I report a bad review instead?

Only when it breaks Google's policies, for example a review from a competitor or a former employee, a fake review, harassment, or one that posts someone's personal information. Google says not to report a review just because you disagree with it, and only reviews that break its policies are removed.

To report it, open your profile, select Read reviews, select Report next to the review, choose the reason and select Send report. Google says the review usually takes several days to be evaluated, and you can follow it in the Reviews Management Tool, where a one-time appeal is possible if no violation is found. Reply calmly in the meantime. More detail is in how to report fake or spam reviews on Google.

What Kabsi does here

Kabsi emails you at once about any review of 3 stars or less, even if you chose WhatsApp for routine messages. A complaint, a refund request or a price complaint gets a careful draft with the issue shown above it, for example "They mention a refund. Kabsi didn't promise one." Every draft points the client to the details on your profile and never contains a phone number, an email or a link.

A review about an allergy, an injury or another safety problem, a legal threat, or a complaint that names a member of your team gets no draft. It is marked "This review needs a little more care" with a short checklist, can never be approved on WhatsApp, and Kabsi writes a short, neutral holding reply only if you ask for one. Kabsi cannot remove a review, and nothing goes on Google until you approve it. Run the free check.

Questions owners ask
Can I offer a free correction if they change their review?
No. Google's policy does not allow incentives, such as discounts or free services, in exchange for revising or removing a negative review. You can offer to put things right privately, with no link to the review.
Should I name the stylist in my reply to a complaint?
No. Reply as the salon, keep the stylist's name out, and deal with what happened in private. A name in a public complaint stays on your profile for every future client to read.
Sources

What should a barbershop post on Google?

Post what a client needs to know before walking in: a photo of a fresh cut, a new barber, walk-in times, a new service or your holiday hours. Use an Update with a Book button for most of it, an Offer only when you have a real offer with dates, and post when something changes.

By Kabsi. Published 7 December 2026. 7 min read

Checked against Google's help pages on 8 November 2026. 
In short
A clear photo of real work, taken with the client's OK, is the simplest post a barber can make.
Updates suit news and walk-in times, Offers need a title and dates, and Events need start and end dates.
Keep phone numbers, emails and social handles out of the text: Google may reject the post.
Google archives posts older than 6 months unless they have a date range.
See what Google shows about you

Find your business on Google
Check my business free

Free check. No account and no Google access needed.

In this guide
1. What is a Google post, and where do clients see it?
2. What should a barber actually post about?
3. What does a good barbershop post look like?
4. What makes a good photo for a barber's post?
5. How often should a barbershop post?
6. How do I post on my Google profile from my phone?
7. Why might Google reject a barber's post?
8. What Kabsi does here

What is a Google post, and where do clients see it?

A post is a short update on your Google profile, with text, a photo or a video, and often a button. Google says clients find posts in the Updates or Overview tab of your profile on a phone, and in the From the owner section on a computer, on both Search and Maps.

Google describes three kinds of post. An Update shares news and can have a description, a photo or video and a button that links to your own website, such as your booking page. An Offer needs a title, dates and times, and gets a View Offer button by itself. An Event needs a title and start and end dates; Google says that without times, it shows as lasting 24 hours on each date. The general guide for every kind of business is Google posts for a local business.

What should a barber actually post about?

Anything true that helps someone choose you or turn up at the right time. For a barbershop that usually means the work itself, the people, when to come in and what is new.

A fresh cut: a skin fade, a beard shape-up or a kids' cut, photographed in good light, with one line about it.
A new barber: their name, what they are good at and the days they work, with their OK.
Walk-ins: which days you take walk-ins and when it is usually quieter.
A new service: a hot towel shave, beard colour, or a longer appointment for textured hair.
Hours that change: late nights before Eid or Christmas, a closed day, a new Sunday opening.
A real offer: a student price on weekdays, with the dates it runs and its terms.
What does a good barbershop post look like?

Short, specific and true, with one clear button. Two or three sentences are enough: what it is, when, and what to do next.

Example: an Update with a Book button

"Jay has joined the team. He specialises in skin fades and beard work, and he is in Tuesday to Saturday. Book with Jay on our page."

Example: an Offer with dates

"Student cut, weekdays before 2pm. Show a valid student card. Runs from 1 to 31 March."

Google's tips are to keep posts professional, with no misspellings, extra characters, text that adds no value or distracting content, and to add a descriptive title, start and end dates and offer details. An offer is between you and your clients: never tie it to leaving a review, which Google's policy does not allow.

What makes a good photo for a barber's post?

A real photo of real work, in focus and well lit. Google asks for photos without significant alterations or excessive use of filters or AI, so that the image represents reality, and a heavy filter on a fade does the opposite.

Do

JPG or PNG, between 10 KB and 5 MB, ideally 720 by 720 pixels or more.
The back and side of the cut, in daylight or under even light.
Ask the client before their face is in the photo.
Your own shop: the chairs, the front, the team at work.

Avoid

Photos taken from another barber's account.
Filters that change the colour of hair or skin.
Screenshots of your social media posts.
A client's face without asking.

Google's content policy treats someone's face in a photograph, posted without their consent, as personal information, so a quick question in the chair saves trouble later. For your profile's own photos, Google suggests at least three photos at work and three team photos. More is in which photos to add to your Business Profile.

How often should a barbershop post?

Google does not set a number. Post when something changes or when you have new work to show, and keep at least one post current, because Google says posts older than 6 months are archived unless a date range is set.

A steady habit is easier than a burst: one new photo of the week's best cut, or a line about next week's hours, is enough. Kabsi does not promise that posting changes where you come up on Google. Posts are there so a client looking at your profile today sees what is true today.

How do I post on my Google profile from my phone?

Sign in to the Google Account linked to your profile, go to your Business Profile and select Posts, then Add post. Choose Update, Offer or Event, add the text, the photo and a button, and select Post.

Go to your Business Profile.
2
Select Posts, then Add post.
3
Choose Update, Offer or Event.
4
Add the text, a photo and, for an Update, a button that links to your booking page.
5
To post later, turn on Schedule this post and choose the date and time.
6

Google checks each post against its content policy. Live means it shows on Search and Maps; Pending means it is still being processed, or your profile is not verified; Not approved means it broke a policy, and the question mark next to the status says which.

Why might Google reject a barber's post?

The usual reason is contact details in the text. Google says it may remove posts with unverified contact information, including phone numbers, email addresses and social media handles, and suggests a Call now button instead, which uses the phone number on your profile.

Google also asks that buttons link only to websites you trust, that posts stay respectful and family friendly, and that businesses in regulated industries do not include content about regulated products. If a post is not approved, fix the part the question mark points to and post it again. Holiday hours themselves belong under Special hours, not only in a post: see Christmas and bank holiday hours on Google for UK salons or UAE National Day and Eid hours on Google for salons.

Before a photo goes up, Kabsi checks it for light, focus, size, a repeat of one you already added and a likely screenshot, and removes the location and other hidden details. It does not check faces, so ask the client first. Each post is checked for phone numbers, emails, links and social handles in the text. Nothing goes on Google until you say yes. Run the free check.

Is it all right to use a stylist's name in my reply?

Yes, when the client named them first and the stylist is happy for it. Google's tips say to personalise a reply and acknowledge the reviewer's specific feedback, and thanking the person they praised does exactly that.

Ask each member of your team once, when they join, whether they are happy to be thanked by name in replies, and use only the first name the client used. Google's content policy treats someone's full name or last name posted without their consent as personal information, so a surname, a personal social account or where they live never belongs in a reply.

Your replies show as your business, not as you, and the reviewer is notified when you reply. Google checks every reply against its content policies before it appears, usually within 10 minutes and sometimes up to 30 days.

How do I reply to praise for a named stylist or barber?

Thank the client, name the stylist once, mention one thing from the review and say you will pass the words on. Google's advice is to keep replies short, conversational rather than promotional, and focused on something real the client said.

Example review, 5 stars: "Maya fixed a colour another salon ruined and actually listened to what I wanted." Reply: "Thank you, Leila. Maya will be so pleased to read this, and we know how much it matters to be listened to after a bad experience. See you next time. Rose Lane Salon"

Example review, 5 stars: "Best fade I have had in years, Sami takes his time." Reply: "Thanks, Chris. I have shown Sami your review. Good to hear the extra minutes are worth it. The Fade Room"

Leave out offers, prices and booking pushes. Google says your reviewers are already customers, so a reply should share a detail that reinforces their experience rather than a deal.

What if the review names someone who has left?

Thank the client for the kind words and say the team appreciates them. Do not say where the stylist has gone or why they left, and do not suggest a replacement in the same breath.

Example reply: "Thank you, Anna, that is lovely to read. Jess is no longer with us, and we will make sure she hears your words. We hope to see you again." If the person left on bad terms, a reply that does not name them at all is fine. Their personal details stay out of public view either way.

How do I reply when a review blames a named stylist?

Reply as the salon, not as the stylist, and leave their name out of your reply. Speak to the stylist privately before you write anything, then thank the client, say you are sorry it went wrong and ask them to get in touch through the details on your profile.

Example review, 1 star: "Emma was rude and rushed my cut. Would not go back." Reply: "We are sorry your visit felt rushed, and thank you for telling us. That is not how we want anyone to feel here. Please get in touch through the details on our profile so the owner can hear what happened. Rose Lane Salon"

Do

Hear the stylist's side in private first.
Apologise for the experience once.
Move the conversation to a phone call or an email.

Do not

Repeat the stylist's name in your reply.
Defend or blame the stylist in public.
Say what the client said or did in the chair.

Google's tips for negative reviews are to protect privacy, avoid personal attacks, be honest and apologise when appropriate. A public argument about a named person helps nobody, and it stays under your profile.

Can I ask clients to mention their stylist in a review?

No. Google's policy says merchants must not ask staff to collect reviews that include specific content, including content that identifies a staff member, and must not ask staff to collect a certain number of reviews. Ask every client for an honest review in the same way, and let them decide what to write.

That rules out cards that say "Mention my name", review counts per chair, prizes for the stylist with the most reviews, and asking only the clients you think were happy. Google's policy also says businesses must not discourage negative reviews or offer incentives, such as discounts or free services, for a review.

What staff can say

"If you have a minute, we would love an honest review on Google. Here is the link." The same words for every client, after every appointment. More is in how to ask customers for Google reviews.
When should I report a review that names a stylist?

When it breaks Google's policies, not when it is simply unfair. Google removes reviews that harass people, post personal information without consent, are fake, or come from a conflict of interest such as a former employee or a competitor.

To report it, open your profile, select Read reviews, select Report next to the review, choose the reason and select Send report. Google says evaluation typically takes several days and that you can follow it in the Reviews Management Tool, with a one-time appeal if no violation is found. While you wait, a calm reply that names no one is still the best thing under the review. The steps for any bad review are in how a salon should reply to a bad Google review.

A reply Kabsi drafts thanks a stylist or a barber by name only when the review names them and they are on your team list; a name that is not on the list is never used, and Kabsi asks you to check the list again after 180 days. A complaint that names a member of your team gets no draft. Your review link and QR code are the same for every client, with no counts per stylist and no targets. Nothing goes on Google until you approve it. Run the free check.

Replies on your profile are posted as the business, and Google does not show the personal name of whoever wrote them. Write as the salon and sign with the salon's name or the owner's.
Can I give the stylist with the most reviews a bonus?
No. Google's policy does not allow asking staff to collect a certain number of reviews, or reviews that identify a staff member. Ask every client the same way and reward your team for their work instead.

Can a client review us over a fee if they never came in?

Usually, yes. Google says a review should reflect a genuine experience with a business, and booking an appointment and being charged a fee is a dealing with your business. Google also says it removes only reviews that break its policies, not ones a business disagrees with.

So a one-star review about a no-show fee is normally one to answer, not one to report. A review is worth reporting only when it breaks a policy, for example when it comes from someone who was never a client, from a competitor or a former employee, or when it harasses a member of staff. The steps are in how to report fake or spam reviews on Google.

How do I reply to a complaint about a no-show fee?

Keep it short and kind. Thank them, say you understand that a fee is frustrating, give the reason for the policy in one sentence, and ask them to get in touch so you can talk about their booking in private.

Example review, 1 star: "Charged me for an appointment I forgot about. Greedy." Reply: "Thank you for your feedback, Dana, and we understand a fee is frustrating. Each appointment holds a technician's time for you, which is why our booking page asks for notice to cancel. Please get in touch through the details on our profile and we will look at your booking together. Polish Nail Bar"

Google's tips for negative reviews include being honest, explaining what you can and cannot do, and apologising when appropriate. Google's own example is a business that cancels an event for bad weather explaining that it sends advance notice when it can. The same idea works here: say why the rule exists, not that the client broke it.

What about a client who arrived late and lost the slot?

Say sorry that the visit did not happen, explain once why a late start cannot always be fitted in, and invite them back. Lash sets, nail extensions and colour need a fixed amount of time, and a calm reply that says so reads as fair to the next client.

Example review, 2 stars: "Ten minutes late and they refused to do my lashes." Reply: "We are sorry your appointment did not go ahead, Nour. A full set needs the whole appointment, and starting late would have meant rushing your lashes or making the next client wait. We would love to see you again, and you can reach us through our profile to rebook. Lash Studio" Write only what is true for your studio. If you sometimes do fit a late client in, say that instead.

How do I reply when we were the ones who cancelled?

Apologise plainly and own it. A salon that cancels on a client and then argues in a reply looks worse than the cancellation itself, so say sorry, give the reason only if it helps, and say what you have changed to avoid it.

Example review, 1 star: "Cancelled my bridal trial the night before." Reply: "You are right to be upset, Grace, and we are sorry. Your stylist was ill and we should have found you another time straight away. Please get in touch through our profile and we will put that right. Rose Lane Salon" Google says a constructive reply and following up on concerns can show you care, and may even encourage the client to update their review. It is their choice whether they do.

What should I never write about a fee in a public reply?

Anything private or anything that sounds like a threat. Google says never to share a reviewer's private information or engage in personal attacks, and its content policy treats financial information about a person as personal information.

Fine in a reply

The reason for your policy, in one sentence.
That the policy is shown when clients book, if it is.
An invitation to get in touch through your profile.

Keep out of a reply

The amount charged, the card or the payment.
How many times they missed or cancelled before.
Debt collection, legal action or a ban.
A refund offered if they change or remove the review.
Should I refund the fee to make the review go away?

Decide the refund on its merits, privately, and never link it to the review. Google's policy says businesses must not offer incentives, such as payment, discounts or free services, in exchange for posting a review or for revising or removing a negative one.

If you refund, refund because it is fair, and say nothing about the review when you do. If the client then updates the review by choice, that is their decision. Asking for it, or making the refund depend on it, is what Google's policy does not allow.

Stop the next review before it starts

Put your cancellation and lateness policy on your booking page and in the booking confirmation, where clients agree to it. Google says a business description can include anything helpful for customers to know, so a line that you work by appointment fits there too.
What Kabsi does here

Kabsi works only with your Google profile: it does not connect to your booking system and does not see who booked or paid. Run the free check.

You can report any review, but Google removes only reviews that break its policies. A client who booked and was charged had a dealing with your business, so a calm reply usually does more.
Should I say the policy was in their confirmation email?
You can say the policy is shown when clients book. Leave out anything about this client's own emails, card or history, which belong in a private conversation.

For a salon: the reception desk, each station, the appointment card and the follow-up message.

How do I get my Google review link and QR code?

On your Business Profile, select Read reviews, then Get more reviews, and select Copy for the link. Google says the QR code can only be made on a computer browser, not on a phone: right-click it and select Save image as.

Customers must be signed in to a Google Account to leave a review, and Google says they can set one up with an email address that is not Gmail. Test the link on your own phone before you print anything. The full walk-through is in how to get your Google review link and QR code.

Where in the shop should the QR code go?

Where clients have a free minute and a phone in hand. Google's own suggestions are on receipts, in thank-you emails, at the end of a chat, and as a QR code printed and displayed in your store. In a salon or a barbershop that means a few fixed places.

Reception and the till: a small card by the card machine, where every client stands once.
Each station: a card by the mirror, where clients wait for colour to develop or for the next barber.
The waiting area: one card on the table, at eye level, not on the floor.
The appointment card and the receipt: the QR code printed small on the back.
The follow-up message: the link in the thank-you message or booking confirmation. Google says you can also send review requests by email, WhatsApp message or a Facebook post.
When is the right moment to ask?

After the work is done, in the same words for every client: at the till, or in the message that follows the visit. Google's policy says businesses should not require or pressure people to leave ratings or write reviews while they are on the premises.

A card on the desk and one friendly line is fine. Handing a client a tablet, waiting while they type, or asking them to review before they leave the chair is the pressure Google's policy describes. A message after the visit gives them time to decide.

The same line for everyone

"If you have a minute, we would love an honest review on Google. The code is on the desk." Every client, every time.
Why can't I ask only the clients who seemed happy?

Because Google's policy says businesses must not discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively ask for positive ones. Choosing who gets the link by how the visit went is exactly that, whether you do it by eye or with a form.

This is often called review gating: asking clients first how their visit was, and sending only the happy ones to Google. Google's own advice is to value all reviews, and it says a mix of positive and negative feedback often feels more trustworthy to people deciding where to go. More is in what review gating is, and why Google does not allow it.

The same policy says merchants must not ask staff to collect a certain number of reviews, or reviews that identify a staff member. So no targets per stylist, no prize for the barber with the most reviews, and no card that says "mention my name".

Can I give a discount or a free product for a review?

No. Google says offering incentives, like free or discounted goods or services, in exchange for posting reviews, changing reviews or removing negative ones is fake engagement and strictly prohibited, and that reviews must reflect a genuine experience.

Allowed

A QR code on the desk and at each station.
The link in every client's follow-up message.
One plain line asking for an honest review.

Not allowed

10 percent off your next cut for a review.
A free product or a prize draw for reviewers.
Sending the link only to clients you think are happy.
Standing over a client while they write it.
What should the card and the message say?

Something neutral that asks for an honest review and nothing more: no stars, no 'five star' and no wording that tells the client what to write. Google's policy says businesses should not request that specific content be included.

On the card: your salon's name, the QR code and "Tell us how your visit went."
2
In the message: "Thank you for coming in today. If you have a minute, tell others how your visit went:" followed by the link.
3
On the website or the booking confirmation: the same link, with the same words.

Keep a spare card behind the desk, and check every few months that the code still opens your own review page. If you change your business name or move, test it again.

What Kabsi does here

Get reviews is free for every business: a short review link and a QR code that open your Google review page, with no rating screen, no filtering and no reward. You can make up to 5 links, for example one for reception and one for the stations, and see how often each was opened. An open is not a review: Google decides which reviews appear. Without signing in, the free review link tool gives you a printable counter card that says "Scan to review us on Google", with no stars.

On WhatsApp, send "ask a customer" and Kabsi sends back one ready message with your link to forward after a real visit, the same for every client. Kabsi never receives your client's number, never messages your clients and keeps no counts per stylist or barber. Run the free check.

Yes, as long as every client gets the same message and nobody is given a target. Google's policy does not allow asking staff to collect a certain number of reviews.

replies.body:
Why does Google show the wrong details for my salon?

Google gathers details from more than you: suggestions from people on Maps, other public sources such as websites, its own automated calls and messages, and booking partners. Open Edit profile to see what Google changed, which shows in blue, then correct it and make your website and booking page say the same.

Anyone can suggest an edit to your salon on Google Maps, and Google may publish it.
Changes made by Google show in blue in your profile editor, with a notice at the top.
A booking link you never added usually comes from a third-party partner, and only that partner can take it off.

Where do the details on my Google profile come from?

Not only from you. Google says it gathers information from different sources, such as user reports and licensed content, and that if those sources report your profile information is incorrect or outdated, Google may update your profile.

Google also says that, in some regions and categories, it may contact the verified phone number on your profile with automated calls, texts or WhatsApp messages to confirm your details, and that what you answer may be used to update your profile. If a junior member of staff answers the salon phone and says you close at 6 on Saturdays, that can end up on Google.

Where it is available, Edit profile, then Collected info, shows the information Google collected this way, with its source and the date it was collected. You can delete an item there, and Google says deleting it removes it from Google's records without changing the other details already on your profile.

How do I see what Google changed on my profile?

Sign in to the Google Account linked to your profile and select Edit profile. Google says that in the profile editor, information changed by Google shows in blue, and that when your profile has Google updates you find a notification at the top of the page.

1
Search your salon's name and town on a phone, signed out, and read it as a client would: hours, phone, address, website and the booking button.
2
Signed in, select Edit profile and look for text in blue and a notice at the top.
3
Open Hours and check both your main hours and your Special hours.
4
Check the email address linked to your profile for messages about suggested edits.

If the wrong detail is your hours, the full steps are in someone changed my hours on Google.

Can clients change my salon's details on Google?

They can suggest changes. Google Maps lets anyone signed in suggest an edit to a place's name, category, address, hours, phone number and website, or report it closed. Google says it reviews all edits, and may tell you about certain suggested edits before they are published.

When Google asks you, by email or in your profile, you have 4 days to accept or reject the suggestion. Google says that if you do not respond in time, it may publish the edit when it is supported by other public information, such as your website, and that in some cases it may apply an edit without asking you, where the edit is needed to meet its policy guidelines.

Your website is your evidence

If your website still shows last year's hours or your old phone number, it can support the wrong suggestion. Update your website and your booking page whenever you change your Google profile.
Why does my profile show a booking link I never added?

Google says links for appointments and reservations can appear on your profile automatically through third-party partners. You cannot delete those yourself in your profile settings: you contact the provider through its opt-out link, support form or account page.

Google says third-party providers are required to process opt-out requests within 5 business days, and that if a provider does not remove the link in that time, you can report a third-party violation. It happens to salons that tried a booking app once and moved on: clients tap the old button and land on a page that is no longer yours.

Your own link is separate. Google lets you add up to 10 links for booking an appointment, and with more than one, Set preferred link marks yours as Business preferred at the top. Tap the booking button yourself on a phone after any change.

Why does Google say my salon is closed?

Check Edit profile, then Hours, first: someone may have marked the business temporarily or permanently closed, or a closure you set may still be on. Google says that if a business is mistakenly marked permanently closed, you can reopen it from your profile.

A rename or a new owner can cause this too. Google Maps tells people who see a new business at a location, or a business whose name changed a lot, to mark the old one permanently closed and add the new one. If you renamed your salon, change the name on your own profile and sign, and Google says you may need to verify again after a name change or a move. If the result is two profiles for one salon, see duplicate Google listings: how to find and fix them.

We only work by appointment. Should we show hours?

Possibly not. Google's guidelines say businesses that operate only by appointment should not provide hours. If clients can walk in during set hours, show them; if every visit is booked, you can choose Open with no main hours under Edit profile, Hours.

A home studio or a room in a shared building with no reception is often appointment only. Hours that do not match reality invite suggested edits from clients who find the door locked. Google also says special hours show only when your hours are set to Open with main hours, so a salon with no main hours uses posts and the booking page for holiday news.

How do I fix the wrong details and keep them right?

Select Edit profile, correct the detail and select Save. Google says it reviews your changes before they go live, so check again a day later, then make sure your website, booking page and social profiles say the same thing.

Answer suggested-edit emails within the 4 days, and check who can edit your profile in Business Profile settings, People and access. Google says owners and managers can both edit information, so an old stylist or agency with access can change details too; see how to remove an old employee or agency from your profile.

Nobody can lock a Google profile or stop people suggesting edits. What works is checking often and answering quickly. More on keeping every site in step is in how to keep your hours and details the same everywhere.

What Kabsi does and does not do here

Once Kabsi is a Manager on your profile, Google Protection checks your business name, phone, website, address, opening hours, main category, open status and map pin every day against the details you confirmed. When Google shows something different, you get one email that explains it, for example "Google shows Sunday closing at 18:00. You approved 22:00.", and says whether Google made the change itself or Kabsi does not know who did. You choose "Google is right" or "Keep my information", and Kabsi never puts anything back by itself.

Kabsi cannot lock your profile or stop suggested edits. It does not edit services, attributes or the booking link on Google today, and it does not connect to booking systems, so a third-party booking link is yours to remove with the provider. Nothing changes on Google until you say so. Run the free check.

Questions owners ask
Can I stop Google changing my salon's details?
No. Google says it may update profiles from other sources and may publish suggested edits. You can answer each suggestion within 4 days, keep your website matching, and correct anything wrong in Edit profile.
How do I remove a booking button from an app I no longer use?
Contact that booking provider through its opt-out link or support form. Google says providers must process the request within 5 business days, and you can report a third-party violation if they do not.
